Subject: MAP & acceptance tests for upcoming pilot

Jonas / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team is excited about Redwood but we need a tightly scoped mutual action plan and a set of acceptance tests before we can sign the pilot SOW. High-level asks from CareGrid:

- Clear functional acceptance criteria (latency, accuracy for triage classification, and hallucination tolerance)
- Evidence we can hand to our security/compliance leads (SOC2 artifacts, data retention logs, audit logging sample)
- An incident/test protocol so our ops team can validate failover/rollback behavior during the pilot
- A proposed timeline that aligns with our procurement window (we need pilot started by 2027-07-15)

Two specific points: 1) we need to know the 95th percentile generation latency SLO you can hold for our expected load (approx 20 concurrent sessions), and 2) how you measure "concordance" for clinical triage (what metric, datasets, and acceptance threshold).

Can you send a draft MAP and a short test matrix this week? We also attached a marked-up SOW (we'll send formally) with a few commercial redlines.

Best,
Jessica Tran
Director of Product Operations

Subject: Re: MAP & acceptance tests for upcoming pilot

Jessica — thanks, and really appreciate the clarity. Draft attached: ‘redwood_caregrid_map_draft.pdf’ and a lightweight test matrix ‘evaluation_test_matrix.xlsx’. Below is the executive summary and proposed acceptance/exit gates.

Executive summary (short):
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference for CareGrid triage assistant across precision/latency/cost tradeoffs and verify operational controls for regulated PHI flows.
- Pilot scope: 6-week evaluation (canary week + 4-week steady-state + final evidence week). Start target: 2027-07-15.

Acceptance criteria (pass = all three domains passed):
1) Reliability & latency:
  - 95th percentile generation latency <= 350ms for 20 concurrent sessions (measured at our edge).
  - Error rate (model runtime failures) < 0.2% over steady-state week.
2) Quality & concordance:
  - Clinical triage concordance: F1 >= 0.88 against the annotated sample set (we propose the CareGrid-200 test set in sheet 2 of the matrix).
  - Hallucination rate (unsupported assertions) < 3% on a 500-case random sample.
3) Security & compliance evidence:
  - Provide SOC2 evidence packet (AICPA report summary) and example retention/audit logs from a simulated request run.

Exit gates (fail/hold conditions):
- If latency > 500ms (95th) for more than 2 hours during steady-state -> automatic rollback to baseline model and immediate postmortem.
- If concordance drops below 0.82 in any continuous 24-hour window -> pause pilot and trigger root cause analysis.
- If PII/PHI leakage / unexpected persisted data observed -> immediate suspension pending forensic review.

Incident/test protocol (short):
- Canary week: synthetic load + targeted adversarial prompts to test hallucination/edge cases. Ops-runbook will execute two injected failures (GPU OOM + region failover) and validate fallback routing, KV cache warm-up, and request replay behavior.
- Test owners: Redwood infra (Jonas) leads failover; Marissa (CS) will coordinate data capture and acceptance evidence. Priyom to review contract redlines and Evelyn to confirm evidence set for SOC2 + data retention.

Timeline (proposal):
- 2027-06-28: Redwood provides final MAP + test artifacts (we can update as we iterate) -> ACTION (Jonas)
- 2027-07-06: Legal & procurement alignment (SOW signoff window) -> ACTION (Priyom + CareGrid legal)
- 2027-07-15: Canary week begins -> ACTION (Jonas / Marissa / CareGrid ops)
- 2027-08-19: Final evidence week + signoff decision -> ACTION (Marissa / CareGrid product)

Notes on measurement: metrics will be collected at both endpoints (CareGrid edge and Redwood telemetry). We'll provide raw logs for the acceptance window and a reconciled report.

Attaching: redwood_caregrid_map_draft.pdf (MAP draft), evaluation_test_matrix.xlsx (detailed test cases + sample sets).

If that looks good, Priyom can start on the SOW redline responses and Evelyn will list the exact artifacts we will hand over for compliance.

Thanks — will follow up with calendar invites once we align.

Jonas Weber
Director, Platform Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Jonas — thanks for the fast turnaround. High level feedback after internal review:

- The acceptance thresholds look reasonable; we'll run the CareGrid-200 and a separate 300-case edge set focused on low-frequency conditions.
- We need explicit verification steps for data deletion at the end of the pilot (retention window mechanics + scrub confirmation).
- The incident/test protocol is great; one ask: can you add an annualized PS estimate for an optional formal forensic replay if we need deeper audit (we might buy that as an add-on).

On the SOW: our legal returned the redlines (attached: CareGrid_SOW_redlines.docx). Key commercial asks: 1) a 30-day termination clause if pilot fails acceptance, 2) liability cap aligned to pilot fees (small), and 3) one-month free extension if evidence week slips due to Redwood-caused outages.

We'd also like to schedule a short runbook tabletop with your ops folks during the canary week — 45 minutes to walk through the injected failure scenarios. Can we tentatively book that for 2027-07-18?

Thanks — Rahul and I are aligned to move quickly once we have confirmation on the deletion checklist and the SOW responses.

Best,
Jessica Tran
Director of Product Operations
CareGrid Health
